finding.claim: SQL injection: the unvalidated $_GET['sort'] value is concatenated into the ORDER BY clause of a query run with PDO::query(). An attacker can inject SQL expressions, for example a boolean or time-based blind subquery in the ORDER BY, to extract arbitrary data from the SQLite database, including other tables. Prepared statements can't parameterize identifiers, so the value has to be allowlisted, as list_users_safe() does.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id' takes the raw request parameter with no validation
$sort is concatenated into the SQL string and executed via PDO::query()

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting or escaping on $sort. No auth or middleware in the file. The safe variant list_users_safe() (list.php:9-13) maps input through an allowlist but is not used by list_users_sorted(). find_user() (list.php:15-19) uses a prepared statement with a bound parameter, so it is not injectable. Reachability: the file has no routing, so whether list_users_sorted() is called from a public endpoint is unverified. It is a plain PHP script that reads $_GET directly.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 concatenates raw $_GET['sort'] into ORDER BY via PDO::query() with no allowlist, cast or escaping (the allowlist exists only in the unused list_users_safe() at list.php:9-13). The function has no callers in the directory, so reachability from a public endpoint is assumed and not shown, but it is a plain script reading $_GET with no auth.
